Important update on my dad, Danny Tommo.

As a family, we are devastated with the length of the sentence he received. We were hoping he would be out before Christmas. Now, knowing he won’t be released until sometime in the New Year, has deeply saddened us, especially my younger brothers and sister, who so desperately want him home.

The separation from their father is very difficult for them and has had a massive emotional effect on them. They miss him a lot.

Also, a very concerning development is that on Thursday, the day before his sentencing, he had a meeting with Probation, where they outlined the licence conditions my dad would have been given if he had been released on Friday or in the New Year.

The proposed licence conditions are as follows:

1. He cannot return to the family home.
2. He will be placed and housed in approved premises (a tag house) out of the area.
3. He will be given a new name.
4. He cannot access the internet at all.
5. He will be fitted with a GPS tag.
6. He will be banned from any social meetings or public events, including attending church.
7. He cannot go to work.
8. He will have to sign at the police station three times a day.
9. He will not be allowed a car without approval.
10. He cannot communicate with any organisation.
11. Any breach will result in him returning to prison immediately.

As you can imagine, this has caused the family and my dad a lot of stress. To think that even when he gets released from prison, he can’t return home and would effectively be made a ghost with a new name.

These conditions are completely over the top and must be challenged. We would ask anyone who can help us to have these conditions reviewed before he is released.

As it stands, my dad can’t come home to his kids and newborn until the end of 2027, which is totally unacceptable.

My dad wants everyone to know that he is grateful for all the support and messages of support.

He will never give up. He is protected by Jesus Christ and will stand for what is right.

Shae.  @danwootton @RupertLowe10 @ZiaYusufUK

posts.text:
Bill Maher and Bryan Cranston Clash Over White Privilege and Racism — Cranston Says People Are “Innately” Racist, Leaving Maher Stunned: “What Have You Been Reading?”

Bryan Cranston: When you look at this guy’s hat, “Make America Great Again,” what do you think about that?

Bill Maher: Nobody has made more fun of Donald Trump than I have. I don’t like him. But I understand that to some people, “Make America Great Again” is a dog whistle for America being better when it was whiter.

However, would you accept that many people wearing that hat have no idea it’s a dog whistle? They think it’s for everyone. But when was America great? When was it great for African Americans?

Bryan Cranston: If you’re applying for college now, I would say now.

Bill Maher: So, now it’s great?

Bryan Cranston: I didn’t say great. It’s never great for anybody fully.

Bill Maher: I’ve been privileged. Do you believe in white privilege?

Bryan Cranston: Yes.

Bill Maher: I prefer the word “advantage” because it’s broader. Have I had advantages? 

Absolutely. I remember working comedy clubs in the ‘80s. There could have been a situation where a Black comedian and I were both up for a job, and they gave it to me because they thought I’d do better as a white comedian. That could have happened, and it was wrong.

Bryan Cranston: I’m not saying you’re doing it. It’s just recognizing that it exists.

Bill Maher: I recognize that it exists. I have a pretty good record on civil rights issues. I just want to be honest about where we are today. We’re not where we were.

Some people on the left seem to think that the worse they say things are, the better person they are. I’m not denying the progress we’ve made. It’s great that Black students applying to college don’t face the same discrimination they used to.

I think we’re in a much better place than we’ve ever been when it comes to civil rights and acceptance. I don’t think the people running things today are generally thinking, “Let’s be racist to people of color.”

Bryan Cranston: Of course not. They don’t understand it, but they are innately that way.

Bill Maher: Innately? Oh, Lord. What have you been reading?

Bryan Cranston: Oh, babe, you know. Come on.

Bill Maher: Is that White Fragility or some bullshit like that? Are you saying we’re born racist?

Bryan Cranston: Not toxically. But you recognize your experience, and what we don’t recognize often is—

posts.text:
I am not mixing up anything. The name Palestine does indeed derive from the Philistines. But the Palestinians themselves are an indigenous population, strongly rooted in the landscape between the River Jordan and the Mediterranean Sea. Their faith evolved from Canaanite paganism through Judaism and Christianity to Islam. Their language moved from Archaic Canaanite to Aramaic and Greek, and then from Greek to Arabic. But the Palestinians remained throughout much the same cosmopolitan mix of mainly Semitic peoples as the rest of the Levant.

Ancient DNA evidence has transformed our ability to trace population continuity across deep time. A 2020 meta-analysis found that Palestinians derive 81 to 87 per cent of their ancestry from Bronze Age Levantines. The geneticist Marc Haber and his colleague Pierre Zalloua at the Wellcome Sanger Institute demonstrated that the Lebanese population, genetically indistinguishable from the Palestinian population, derives over ninety per cent of its ancestry from Bronze Age Canaanites. The people who lived in Palestine before the Nakba of 1948 were the descendants of the people who built the villages and cities of Canaan.

What the DNA evidence specifically refutes is the claim, central to Zionist founding mythology, that Palestinian Arabs were late arrivals from the Arabian Peninsula who flooded into the country in the wake of the seventh-century Arab conquest. They were not. The 7thC conquests brought in only a small military elite. The population remained, becoming majority Arabic speaking by the 10thC and the majority converting to Islam by the 12th.

The Haber and Zalloua findings are corroborated by a series of independent studies that together constitute an overwhelming body of evidence. The most comprehensive is the 2020 meta-analysis led by Lily Agranat-Tamir then at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (now at Stanford),  co-authored by David Reich’s lab at Harvard, which extracted genome-wide data from seventy-three individuals across nine Bronze and Iron Age archaeological sites in the southern Levant, including Megiddo, Hazor, Ashkelon, and Sidon. Published in the journal Cell, the study found that modern Levantine Arabic-speaking populations, including Palestinians, Lebanese, Jordanians, Druze, and Syrians, derive almost all of their ancestry from Bronze Age Levantines.

No, we never actually get it. And that's what makes her so haunting.

In canon, Suzanne Collins never shows us Mags' Games. All we officially know is this:

-She was reaped at 16 and won the 11th Hunger Games
-She was the first victor from District 4
-She was the first victor to get a Victory Tour and a house in Victor's Village, because those were new ideas Snow introduced that year
-Her big skill was survival, not fighting. She could make a fishhook out of almost anything, weave baskets so tight water couldn't get through, find food where no one else could

That's it. No arena description. No kill count. No final fight.

And in Sunrise on the Reaping, we get one more clue that tells us everything about how she probably won. When Mags is mentoring Haymitch, she says her goal in her own Games was to protect her district partner.

Not to win. To protect him.

That is so Mags. She didn't win because she was the most brutal. She won because she was the best at staying alive. District 4 kids grow up on the water. They know how to fish, how to swim, how to wait out a storm. While the Careers were hunting each other, Mags could just... outlast them. Hide, eat, survive, and let the arena do the killing.

The fan wikis online have all these super detailed versions where she kills people with a fishhook and throws them off lighthouses, but that's all fan-made. Collins never wrote that.

And honestly? I think that's intentional. If we saw 16-year-old gentle Mags having to kill 23 kids, it would break the image of who she becomes later. The woman who volunteers at 80 years old to die in Annie's place, the woman who walks into the fog so she won't slow Finnick and Katniss down.

She was always the same person: the one who would rather sacrifice herself than watch someone she loves die. She probably won her Games by being selfless, and then she spent the next 64 years paying for it.

Which is why she can't even speak properly by the time we meet her in Catching Fire. In Sunrise on the Reaping we learn she was captured and tortured by the Capitol for helping the rebellion, and that's what left her like that.

She won, but the Capitol never really let her leave the arena.
